Extract a tidy estimates frame from a fitted RdistNN object

Source: R/plot-data.R, R/user-dnn-affine-ratio-methods.R
plot_data_estimates.Rd

Returns one row per target point and coefficient with the point estimate, stored standard error, and symmetric pointwise normal confidence bounds. The uncertainty calculation follows the estimator: jackknife for NP/CATE, paired-score linearization for ratios, and sandwich inference for GMM or density-backed PLQR coefficients. This is the data layer of the plotting interface: plot builders consume these frames, and users can consume them directly for custom figures.

Usage

plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, ...)

# Default S3 method
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'np_result'
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, candidates = "default", ...)

# S3 method for class 'cate_result'
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, candidates = "default", ...)

# S3 method for class 'plqr_result'
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, quantity = c("moment", "theta"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'gmm_result'
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
plot_data_estimates(object, level = 0.95, candidates = "default", ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted result object (np_result, cate_result, affine_ratio_result, clate_result, plqr_result, or gmm_result; tdnn_np_result dispatches through np_result).

level

Confidence level for the normal bounds (default 0.95).

...

Passed to methods; not used.

candidates

For grid-aware methods, "default", "all", or a character vector of stored candidate ids.

quantity

For plqr_result fits, which quantity to extract: "moment" (default) uses the localized PLQR moments and their jackknife moment_se; "theta" uses the supplied coefficient values (repeated theta_eval) and the direct-sandwich theta_se. While no root solver exists, moments are the target-specific quantity, so they are the default. The choice is recorded in attr(., "quantity").

Value

A data.frame with columns target_id (integer, 1..m), coef (character; "mu"/"tau"/"theta" for scalar fits, moment or coefficient names for vector fits), estimate, se, ci_lower, ci_upper, and — when the fit stores evaluation points — target coordinates x0_1..x0_p, with the original covariate names recorded in attr(., "x0_names"). Fits without stored standard errors return NA in se and the bound columns. The confidence level is recorded in attr(., "level"). Ratio fits also retain unavailable Wald bounds as NA when the ratio is undefined or its score variance is zero.

Experimental methods

Methods for plqr_result objects are experimental, as is all PLQR functionality in this release; see plqr_dnn().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 60
x_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2)
y_vec <- x_mat[, 1] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
fit <- np_dnn(
  X = x_mat, X0 = rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0)), Y = y_vec,
  k = 1L, s = 10L, se = FALSE
)
plot_data_estimates(fit)
#>   target_id coef    estimate se ci_lower ci_upper x0_1 x0_2
#> 1         1   mu 0.002292107 NA       NA       NA    0    0
#> 2         2   mu 0.832118414 NA       NA       NA    1    0
